newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW-Riksbank cuts deposit/lending rates.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Riksbank cuts deposit/lending rates.

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank on Thursday cut its deposit and lending rates by 50 basis points to 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent respectively.
TOMAS POUSETTE, ECONOMIST AT NORDBANKEN
The cut was expected with both low inflation expectations and low inflation faciliating it.
This might possibly be the last corridor cut as it allows the Riksbank to cut the repo rate by 60 basis points, which is a fairly large manouvering room.
Nordbanken expects the repo rate to bottom out around 4.0 percent in the first half of next year.
The repo rate (currenty 4.35 percent) could also be lowered below 4.0 percent as inflation expectations are lower than the Riksbank target average of two percent.
JAMES MCKAY, ECONOMIST AT PAINEWEBBER
This is a clear signal that the Riksbank intends to continue to cut the repo rate. Fundamentals remain extremely supportive, highlighted by the current deflationary conditions.
Furthermore, most of the easing initiative since the start of the year has been offset by currency strength and falls in inflation, leaving monetary conditions vitually unchanged.
Expect futher rate cuts in the weeks ahead, the next repo rate likely on December 17.
The repo is likely to bottom just below four percent in the first quarter.
SVEN-ARNE SVENSSON, ECONOMIST AT HAGSTROMER & QVIBERG
This was expected.
We had targeted a cut of between 25 and 50 basis points.

The Swedish economy looks very good at the moment with the world's lowest inflation, a large trade surplus and a budget deficit that will, according to (government think-tank) KI's Wednesday report, meet Maastricht criteria already this year.
JAMES STEWART, S-E-BANKEN ECONOMIST

I think it (repo cut) is pretty well placed into the market that we'll see a 20 to 25 basis point cut (on December 17). I think the interesting question is where will the repo bottom out? We think the repo rate is likely to bottom out at around the 3.75 percentage level.
However, if you look at the inflation performance in the Swedish economy, it's a very, very strong performance.

If you look at inflation expections of the central bank's Prospera inflation expectations survey, if look at independent forecasters expections...add to that a very tight ficsal stance then I think there are very good reasons to see an easier monetary policy stance.

That's not to say there are no problems, there are. There are still some problems in the economy that might give the central bank some concern but basically the outlook is extremely positive for lowering the repo rate further.
-- Stockholm newroom +46-8-700 1017
